title: The quasi-finite locus is open
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Using quasi-finiteness in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite], the set of points of $X$ at which $f$ is quasi-finite is an open subset $U\subseteq X$, and the induced morphism $U\to S$ is locally quasi-finite.

proof.text: At a point x where f is quasi-finite, unpack Definition 01TD to obtain affine opens U containing x and V with f(U) contained in V. The induced ring map on sections is finite type and quasi-finite at primeIdealOf(x).

source.place: Tag 01TI, first two sentences of proof

proof.text: Use the openness assertion of the finite-type ring-map quasi-finite locus theorem for the affine pair. Its image under the canonical open immersion fromSpec is open in X. The identities range_fromSpec and fromSpec_primeIdealOf, together with injectivity of the chart, show that this open contains x and every point in it is quasi-finite for f using the original affine pair. Thus every point of the locus has an open neighbourhood contained in the locus, proving openness.

source.place: Tag 01TI, proof using Algebra Tag 00QA directly in Spec(A)

proof.text: Let T be this open locus. The induced morphism T -> S is locally of finite type. For x in T choose its finite-type affine pair U,V from Definition 01TD. Restrict U -> V to the open inverse image of U in T. This restricted map is an open immersion followed by U -> V, so is locally of finite type. Mathlib arrowResLEAppIso transports finite type of the ring map to U -> V, and the pointwise restriction criterion for locally finite type finishes.

source.place: Tag 01TI, final assertion, with the local finite-type part of Definition 01TD

proof.text: The affine quasi-finiteness witness at x gives Mathlib quasi-finiteness of the stalk map: identify the fibre-ring singleton with the singleton in the topological affine fibre, use Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.of_isOpen_singleton_fiber, and identify the stalk map with the map between prime localizations using arrowStalkMapIso. Cancel the source localization map using RingHom.QuasiFinite.of_comp. Transfer this stalk-map predicate across the open immersion T -> X. Since T -> S is locally of finite type by the previous step, Mathlib quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_asFiber gives an isolated fibre point. Choose affine source and target neighbourhoods in T and S and apply the isolated-fibre-point affine-pair theorem to obtain the finite-type quasi-finite ring map required by Definition 01TD. This proves local quasi-finiteness of T -> S.
